surfaces.blocked_reason: The page structurally cannot carry a genuine mnemonic-widget GtkLabel. (1) It contains exactly two GtkLabels and neither can honestly hold one: 'empty' has no `label` property at all — it is a pure spacer occupying grid cell (0,4) beside the warning banner, i.e. exactly the invisible/pointless label the brief forbids; 'warningmsg' is `no-show-all=True` and its text is supplied at runtime by MacroSecurityLevelTP::SetWarningLabel (xmlsecurity/source/dialogs/macrosecurity.cxx:183), a hidden warning banner, not a label for any control. (2) All four focusable widgets are GtkRadioButtons (vhigh/high/med/low) whose own inline labels already carry their mnemonics (_Very high, H_igh, _Medium, _Low), so no focusable widget lacks a name a companion GtkLabel would supply; a mnemonic-widget aimed at one radio would create a LABEL_FOR to a single member, which is the wrong a11y construct for a radio group and is predicate-cosmetic. (3) The canon prescribes no static text to add here: docs/design/08-dialogs.md §8.11 'Tabbed surfaces' names SecurityLevelPage explicitly and says it applies the 8.2 Options notebook anatomy 'as embedded page composition, not redraw', and §8.10.4 defers the macro-security-level dialogs to a build host as a documented deferral — so a new heading/supporting line would be UI the canon declines. (4) It would also break layout: the root grid is `row-homogeneous=True`, so a new heading row would be stretched to the tallest (3-line radio) row height, and turning row-homogeneous off would break the upstream bottom-anchored warning banner, which relies on homogeneous rows plus the 'empty' spacer and warningbox `valign=end` to sit at the page bottom (VclGrid::setAllocation, vcl/source/window/layout.cxx:1252 — with no vexpanding row, non-homogeneous rows keep natural height and the banner would ride up under the last radio). The other three prongs already pass (content_grid_material True, ellipsize_count 1, has_own_action_widgets False); only the mnemonic-widget prong is unreachable without inventing UI.
